summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for later lookup; not commentary)

## BOOK 1 of 2: TOMMY by Joseph Hocking (Gutenberg #24986)

**Front matter:** Author note says the story is partly fact; Hocking addressed recruiting meetings, visited training camps, France/Flanders (La Bassee, Neuve Chapelle, Ypres). Dedicated to fathers/mothers of men in khaki. Signed "Priors' Corner, Totteridge, Herts, February 1916."

**Setting:** Brunford, a Lancashire cotton manufacturing town. Thorn and Thistle public-house (landlord Enoch Powell). Dixon Street (Tom's home). Scott's Park. Liverpool Road. St. George's Street. Mechanics' Institute. Bull and Butcher hotel. Rose and Crown club. Black Cow pub (army town).

**Characters:**
- **Tom Pollard** – protagonist, weaver's son, ~23 in 1914; father **Ezekiel Pollard** (weaver, 30s/wk); mother **Martha (Mrs.) Pollard**, dialect-heavy, sharp-tongued.
- **Polly Powell** – buxom, bold-eyed, highly coloured dresses, feathered hats; daughter of landlord Enoch Powell; later walks out with Jim Dixon, Jim Scott, Jim Parkin mention.
- **Alice Lister** – refined, contralto singer, pianist, daughter of George Lister (small manufacturer, ex-weaver) and Mrs. Lister; attends Sunday School/Young Men's Class; Tom's first love.
- **Emily Bilson** – girl who taunts Tom.
- **Harry Waterman** – son of a "squire" in Warwickshire (claimed), educated in Germany; real name secretly German; Tom's social patron; later a German spy; enlisted as officer (Lieutenant/Captain, staff officer).
- **Robert Penrose** – Cornish, Charterhouse-educated, private in Tom's company, later commissioned; Y.M.C.A. goer; refuses commission at first; later Lieutenant who arrests Waterman.
- **Alec McPhail** – Scots, Black Watch, whisky drinker, Colonel Ingersoll reader, dies of wounds at hospital near Ypres (road to Cassel) after conversion; mother in Highlands.
- **Elijah Butterworth** – father of three soldier sons, calls Tom coward.
- **Nick** – Brunford man met in trenches (football).
- **Colonel Blount**, **Major Blundell**, **Sergeant Ashworth**, **General Withers** (Divisional HQ), **Captain Winfield**, **Lieutenant Jackson**, **Brigadier**.
- **Mr. Shweitzer** – German businessman in Brunford; dinner at Bull and Butcher; punched by Englishman after saying Kaiser will rule England.
- **Jim Bates, Arthur Wadge, Bill Perkins, George Wilson** – Tom's pals killed.
- **Mr. Skelton** – young minister who proposes to Alice; refused.
- **Harry Briarfield** – manufacturer's son, Sunday School teacher; proposes to Alice; she delays; (mother's letter falsely says engaged).

**Chronology:**
- Ch I (Sunday, first in June 1914): Tom at Thorn and Thistle; Polly's invitation; Tom with Alice Lister walking from Sunday school; ultimatum "Choice": Alice vs. Thorn and Thistle; Tom chooses Polly, goes drinking. Mother scolds ("Bein' fools runs in the family").
- Ch II: Summer 1914 war news; Austria's ultimatum; Sir Edward Grey; Shweitzer dinner incident; Tom doesn't enlist; Polly discourages him. Jan 1915 (New Year) recruiting meeting at Mechanics' Institute; Tom shouts "By God, no!" and gives his name. Mother: "Lancaster asylum" quip.
- Ch III: Tom tells Polly at midnight; meets Alice next morning, she praises him. Joins Loyal North Lancashires (battalion not named), at a Lancashire town ~30 miles from Brunford. Drunk and disorderly; punished by colonel; Penrose urges Y.M.C.A.; French lessons ("Je suis, Vous êtes, Nous sommes, Ils sont"). McPhail episode. Battalion moves to Surrey camp (May); Penrose reveals Charterhouse; Tom meets Waterman (now lieutenant) in camp.
- Ch IV: Camp life; Tom's letter from mother about Polly ("Look at the stock"); Alec's conversion; farewell meeting at Y.M.C.A., speaker says Christ; canteen scene; Folkestone embarkation; troop train; Boulogne; first gun sounds.
- Ch V: Ypres salient; sergeant describes Wipers battles, gas, German officer shoots rescuer; Tom in trenches; Piccadilly/Haymarket/Bond Street/Whitehall trench names; boy shot by sniper; big bombardment; bayonet charge; German officer shoots young Englishman after drink; Tom prays "O God!"; Waterman seen as staff officer.
- Ch VI: Alice's perspective: refuses young Mr. Skelton; Harry Briarfield proposes; she asks for three days; parents' argument; she prays at midnight, same time Tom prays.
- Ch VII: Night of German shouted warning ("attack at six o'clock to-morrow, eleven hundred strong"); Tom reports to subaltern; attack thwarted by Black Watch; Colonel's cross-questioning; Tom's conversion/assurance of God. McPhail dying at hospital; Tom sings "Jesu, Lover of my soul"; recites Psalm 23; McPhail dies next day ("It's a' richt").
- Ch VIII: Treachery investigation (Colonel Blount, Major Blundell, General Withers). Tom suspicious of Waterman; sees him throw white paper toward German lines; Tom grapples Waterman, Penrose intervenes; Tom crawls into No Man's Land, fights German for paper, breaks his shoulder with football trick; wounded in left arm and right shoulder; delivers paper. Blount: court-martial.
- Ch IX: Court-martial; Waterman admits being German ("Yes" to being German; spelling of name with two n's); shot at dawn at a wall. Tom recommended for D.C.M.
- Ch X: Newspapers "Heroism of a Lancashire Lad"; Tom home on leave in December; Brunford crowds; Polly not wanted; family prays together.
- Ch XI: Tom at chapel with parents; meets Alice outside church; reconciles; Alice not engaged to Harry Briarfield; Tom says he'll work for her after war. Station departure at Waterloo; Kipling's "ship that found herself" reference; narrator sees him off.

**Key quotes/motifs:** "Make your choice"; "Choice" between Alice and Thorn and Thistle; "O God!"; "It's a' richt"; Psalm 23 recited; hymn "Jesu, Lover of my soul"; "Lancaster asylum"; "Methody parson"; "religious lolly-pops"; "Look at the stock" (mother's letter); "au revoir"; "the light of love, and duty, and faith, and chastened joy."

## BOOK 2 of 2: THE YELLOW HOUSE; MASTER OF MEN by E. Phillips Oppenheim (Gutenberg #41402), Volume One

**Narrator:** Kate Ffolliot (daughter of Rev. Horace Ffolliot, new curate-in-charge at Northshire village; sister **Alice** (plain, prim, literal, does parish work); mother's identity revealed later; narrator educated in Berlin and Heidelberg, lived abroad; took Heidelberg degree).

**Other places/people:**
- **Lady Naselton** (Amy Naselton) of Naselton Hall; husband Lord Naselton; son **Fred Naselton** (friend of Berdenstein in Rio). Gossip-monger, matchmaker.
- **The Countess** of Sysington Hall; **Holgates** of Holgate Brand; **Romneys** (Lady Romney); **Lady Applecorn**; **Lady Bolton**; **Mr. Hewitt** (schools, ventilators); **Harrison** (tenant farmer, traps); **Charlsworth** (churchwarden, Mr. Charlsworth); **Morris** (servant/gardener? "Morris gave me the letters" – a servant); **Mary** (housemaid); **Colonel Dacre** (old busybody, Belchester); **Bishop of Exchester** (visits; later Eastminster).
- **Bruce Deville** – of Deville Court; ~mid-30s? (godson of Lady Naselton); tall, broad, ragged beard, untidy clothes, grey eyes, beagles (dog "Lawless" with broken leg, dog "Marvel", "Madam"); ex-"Philip Maltabar"? no—Bruce Deville; had spent fortune on singer Marie Leparte; rescued Olive Berdenstein from carriage accident near Baeren (Lake region); calls "Mr. Deville". Son of Bromley Deville (executor). Father's oldest friend was Adelaide's father.
- **Adelaide Fortress** (Mrs. Fortress) – lives at Yellow House; journalist, Socialist, Dresden cups; formerly lover of Horace; mother of Kate; actual name changed; Bruce's childhood friend (5 years younger).
- **Stephen Berdenstein** – South American (Rio) returned; wealthy; wanted Adelaide; killed by Horace (Philip Maltabar) in plantation near the Yellow House; dying in church shouting "Judas!"; found in church porch.
- **Olive Berdenstein** – his sister, short, dark, thin, sallow, prominent white teeth, diamonds, sealskin coat; in love with Bruce; made compact with Kate; later reveals she is Stephen's sister; came to Eastminster, exposed father; at Colville Hall recognised he was not the man; later "I forgive. Farewell."
- **Philip Maltabar** – alias of Horace Ffolliot in youth; enmity with Stephen since boyhood.
- **Canon Ffolliot** – Horace's new title at Eastminster.
- **Marcia** – Adelaide's name in Horace's first encounter ("Marcia").

**Events in order:**
1. Oct 1st weeks: Kate and father move into Vicarage in Northshire; callers. Lady Naselton gossips about "Yellow House" woman and Bruce Deville (called "failure", "brutal"). Father faints in garden after hearing voice (Adelaide's) in the lane; Bruce passes with beagles.
2. Bruce Deville visits to bandage dog Lawless; quarrel with Horace; Horace: "I desire no welcome from you." Bruce: "That man was closely... associated with the most unhappy chapter of my life."
3. Kate visits Yellow House (storm); meets Adelaide (Socialist; electioneered for Mr. Densham at Belchester); tea; Horace bursts in and orders daughter out; "Marcia!" Horace's cry.
4. Horace receives letter from South America (with "London about fifteenth"); goes to London; Bruce drops envelope same handwriting.
5. Lady Naselton's tea: millionaire **Berdenstein** (Stephen) introduced; reveals Rio; "Adelaide Fortress" is his love.
6. Horace fails to return Friday; Kate goes to Yellow House at night; Adelaide and Bruce evasive; Kate reveals Berdenstein name; Bruce: "He is at Naselton Hall." Horace returns, seen with revolver at plantation.
7. Horace ill; Sunday sermon "The wages of sin"; dying man (Stephen) comes into church, shouts "Judas!"; dies in churchyard; verdict murder; Bishop's remark on sanctuary.
8. Kate ill for a week; Horace made Canon; he tells Kate to promise silence; she goes to Dresden plan; Horace leaves for Eastminster.
9. Sister Olive Berdenstein visits Vicarage; photograph in Adelaide's cabinet of Philip Maltabar (Horace); Kate learns Adelaide is her mother and Horace her father.
10. Kate engaged as Adelaide's secretary (£60/yr); Horace's bandages and bloodied wound; Horace vanishes after telegram; letter from "London"/Ventnor.
11. Olive proposes compact: Kate avoids Bruce; Bruce then proposes to Kate at Vicarage; Kate lies ("I do not care for you").
12. Kate sees Horace in Whitechapel (Commercial Road), who waves her off; mother and Kate go to Colville Hall (mission hall); Horace preaches farewell to East End audience.
13. Eastminster: Bruce proposes again, kisses Kate; Olive interrupts with threats. Evensong: Olive recognises Horace; Horace confesses killing Stephen in self-defence (Stephen's knife wound); Olive goes to police.
14. Horace leaves letter for Kate; at station Olive says detective will meet Horace's train; Bruce at station; they follow; Horace preaches at Colville Hall; collapses (dying); Olive: "I forgive. Farewell." Horace: "This is happiness." Final words.

**Notable phrases:** "Marcia!"; "The wages of sin is death"; "Judas! you, Judas! Oh! my God!"; "It's a' richt" (Tommy, not Yellow House); "I am the victim"; "Ten thousand pounds, and safety for Philip Maltabar"; "This is happiness."

**Transcriber's notes (end):** typos corrected in printed original (e.g., "Berdentein"→"Berdenstein", "nonense"→"nonsense").
